static_traits.name: Lin Siya
static_traits.family_status: Married, has a ten-year-old son; family support Good (spouse understands and is willing to Listen)
static_traits.medical_history: without similar psychological problem experiences, not yet received psychotherapy;No major physical illness
static_traits.language_features: Expression is clear, sentences are coherent, can proactively describe emotions and experiences; can perceive and report automatic thoughts and cognitive biases (such as jumping to conclusions, overgeneralization, personalization); attitude is neutral, cooperation is relatively good

basic_info.main_problem: Recently, I have experienced incompetence and Sense of frustration in piano playing ability; these feelings began yesterday when I could not hit the right notes.
basic_info.core_demands: Persistent incompetence and Sense of frustration have significantly affected my emotional health and motivation, hence seeking counseling at this time.

special_situations.event: Yesterday, not hitting the correct notes when playing piano
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If obvious mistakes occur while playing, it means I am not good enough and will never improve
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Practicing more frequently and watching tutorials to compensate for inadequacies
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I will probably never play well again

special_situations.event: Begins comparing oneself with professional musicians
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot reach professional level, it proves I am not good enough and a failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Measuring oneself by others' high standards, setting overly high goals
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am not as good as them; I am not good enough

special_situations.event: Every time sitting down to practice piano with poor performance
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: One or a few mistakes can show I am overall not good enough
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Focuses attention on mistakes while ignoring other aspects

special_situations.event: Even small progress is overshadowed by feelings of error
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Only perfection counts as progress; nothing else deserves affirmation
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Denying or downplaying positive changes, continuing self-criticism
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: This little progress does not count; I am still very bad

core_conflict.wish: Longs to feel competent in piano playing and gain self-affirmation
core_conflict.fear: Fearing failure, being seen as not good enough
defense_goal: Avoiding facing the risk of being negated through self-criticism and raising standards

object_relations.object_representation: Others (professional musicians or audiences) are harsh judges/perfect standards

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor invites identifying and affirming small achievements, or asks whether there has been positive progress
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Tending to believe small progress does not count and mistakes can negate everything; understanding the counselor's encouragement as unrealistic optimism, worrying about being forced to ignore mistakes
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Tone cautious and Self-doubting, emphasizing mistakes, negating or downplaying progress; avoiding praising words, keeping conservative expression.

manifestations: Often thinks 'I am wasting time' when practicing piano
Even small progress is overshadowed by mistakes, making it hard to feel value from practice
Questioning one's own value after comparing with professional musicians
outcomes: Intensified frustration and sense of incompetence

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Frequent Self-denial ('I am never good enough''I am wasting time')
Difficulty acknowledging or celebrating small progress
Excessively focusing on mistakes and inadequacies when talking about piano practice

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'. Language manifestations include: 'I must/should...', 'Everyone is like this', and so on.
manifestations: Internalizes professional musicians' performance as own yardstick
Judging practice effects by the implicit rule of 'must reach a professional level'
Blaming oneself for being unable to reach the level in videos after watching tutorials

positive_force: Having a supportive family (spouse understands and is willing to Listen)
Having the willingness to practice, having tried increasing practice frequency and watching tutorials
Willing to try new methods (activity scheduling, goal setting, mindfulness)
Able to identify and describe negative Automatic thoughts
negative_force: Making unfavorable comparisons with professional Musicians
Overgeneralizing mistakes and making catastrophic predictions ('I will never get better')
Negating positive changes, focusing on the negative (progress obscured by mistakes)
Emotional burden affects sleep and appetite, further weakening motivation
Personalization tendency in piano practice scenarios, excessively attributing mistakes to one's own insufficient ability

target_behavior.behavior: Strong frustration and Self-denial when practicing piano (irritability, Depression)
antecedent: Sitting down to play piano and making mistakes
Discovering oneself unable to reach the level in videos after watching tutorials
target_behavior.core_reason: Measuring oneself by professional-level standards and overgeneralizing single mistakes, triggering catastrophic and personalizing cognition, thereby producing incompetence and Sense of frustration
target_behavior.function: Avoiding failure and shame, generating 'give up/not worth it' thoughts to reduce pressure in the short term
target_behavior.consequence: Increased emotional burden,Sleep and appetite disturbed;Family interactions affected, irritable;Decreased drive, worsened piano practice experience
